chapter: Cab Calloway, Lunceford, Hampton and Armstrong, 1941-45
title: Glaser asks McRae to build a new band for Louis Armstrong
summary: Glaser sent him to hear Armstrong's band and told him to rebuild it; Welburn lists the new personnel.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: We always wound up down at the Cafe Society -- all down that way. And sometimes when Walter (inaudible), it would be like Joe Glaser, Jack Robbins, Walter Winchell and myself. Now Jack would come -- and it was Jack (inaudible) Glaser. (chuckles) Jack would come with these two fine chicks on his arm, you know. Jack Robbins was a sporty, (inaudible). Come with these two fine chicks on his arm. And we go around and do 52nd Street, sit around and talk, watch (inaudible), you know. And that summer, Joe Glaser called me up and say, "I want you to go down to Norfolk -- Wilmington, Delaware." what do yo' know what's I say, "(inaudible) down there?" He say, "Louie Armstrong is playing down there. I want you to go down there."

He say, "I want you to go and take a listen to that band. I'm think about building a new band." I want you to build them a new band."
He says now, "Come down to the office. I'm gonna give you tickets and money and go down there and tell Frenchie everybody's on notice. Give everybody a two weeks notice."
I say, "You tell Frenchie, I ain't firing nobody."
I say, "You tell Frenchie, I ain't firing -- (inaudible) all those guys in the band. (Inaudible), you know."
So he sent Frenchie a letter and told Frenchie (inaudible) break the band up. He says, "I don't want nobody in the band."
I says, "I don't want to take the band over and have to reset the band up again. It'll be some hard feelings."
I says -- he say, "I want you to build Louie an entire new band." This is the band -- the picture that I showed you (inaudible). Got some of the guys (inaudible) and all them boys. (Inaudible)
